name: Crop is clamped to the image and blanks everything outside it on save, including the last row and column
given: A 1000x800 image (width=1000, height=800) is open in single view (sequence view behaves identically; multi-view has no crop at all). At least one segment exists, so a save will write files. The Border Crop panel takes two text ranges rather than two corners: X = "-10:1200" and Y = "50:700", i.e. corners (-10, 50) and (1200, 700). Each half is parsed as a plain integer with no range validation, and the widget swaps a reversed pair before handing (x1, y1, x2, y2) to the crop manager (border_crop_widget.py:115-135).
when: The crop is applied - either typed into the panel, or drawn by dragging a rectangle that is strictly wider than 5 AND strictly taller than 5 image pixels - and the image is then saved through the single-view/sequence save path (save_export_manager.py:97-122).
then: The crop is stored as (x1, y1, x2, y2) = (0, 50, 999, 700). x is clamped to [0, width-1] = [0, 999], so -10 becomes 0 and 1200 becomes 999; y is clamped to [0, height-1] = [0, 799], so 50 and 700 pass through unchanged; no swap is needed (crop_manager.py:131-140). The X field is rewritten to "0:999", the Y field to "50:700", and the toast reads exactly "Crop applied: 0:999, 50:700" (crop_manager.py:148, 152). On save, the export mask tensor of shape (800, 1000, numClasses), dtype uint8, is COPIED, and in the copy every pixel outside rows [50, 700) x columns [0, 999) is set to 0 in every channel: rows 0-49 cleared across the full width, rows 700-799 cleared across the full width, and, within the surviving rows 50-699, column 999 cleared (the left band [0, x1) is empty here because x1 = 0). Exactly 650 rows x 999 columns = 649,350 pixel positions per channel survive. The row at index y2 (700) and the column at index x2 (999) are themselves cleared: the END COORDINATES ARE EXCLUSIVE, the start coordinates inclusive.
and: Because the clamp is inclusive (x2 <= width-1, y2 <= height-1) while the slice ends are exclusive, the image's last column (index 999) and last row (index 799) can NEVER survive while any crop is active - not even for the maximum crop (0, 0, 999, 799), which keeps only rows 0-798 and columns 0-998. The blanking runs on a copy of the tensor (file_manager.py:720), so the in-memory segments are untouched and clearing the crop restores full-image saves. All exported coordinates stay in the FULL-image frame: the tensor keeps its full (height, width) shape, exporters normalize by the full width/height (e.g. yolo_detection.py:20, 29-32), and no exporter ever reads the crop rectangle itself (it is only a dead field, exporters/__init__.py:107). Per-object exports intersect each segment with the already-cropped tensor (segment_manager.py:297), so YOLO/COCO/VOC/CreateML boxes shrink to the kept region. The crop belongs to the current image only: loading any other image clears it, and it must NOT be restored for a later image of the same dimensions.
parameters: Input: x1, y1, x2, y2 in image pixels, integers. TEXT PATH - each field is "start:end"; each half is parsed as an integer with no range check (negatives and values past the image edge are accepted), then the pair is swapped if reversed (border_crop_widget.py:115-135). DRAG PATH - the rectangle is built from normalized scene coordinates, which are image pixels, not screen pixels (single_view_mouse_handler.py:264); the press must land inside the image but the drag may leave it (:106-110); it is accepted only if rectWidth > 5 AND rectHeight > 5 (strictly greater, both axes, evaluated on the FLOAT rectangle BEFORE truncation and clamping, single_view_mouse_handler.py:553); its edges are then converted by TRUNCATION TOWARD ZERO, not rounding (Python int(), :554-555), so a drag edge at 999.7 becomes 999. Typed coordinates bypass the >5 check entirely. CLAMP - x1, x2 = max(0, min(x, width-1)); y1, y2 = max(0, min(y, height-1)) (crop_manager.py:131-134). ORDER - swap so x1 <= x2 and y1 <= y2 (crop_manager.py:137-140); a no-op on every live path because both entry paths already order the pair. KEPT REGION in the mask - rows [y1, y2) x columns [x1, x2), both ends EXCLUSIVE, across all channels (file_manager.py:724-737). DO NOT PORT the legacy per-image-size crop memory (crop_manager.py:144-145) or its restore-on-load (file_navigation_manager.py:227-238): both are unreachable in the shipping app and the decision is that a crop never carries over. Implement truncation toward zero on the drag path and integer parsing on the text path; never a round-half rule - the legacy round() at crop_manager.py:127 is a documented no-op because both callers already pass integers, and Python's round() is half-to-even, which JavaScript's Math.round does not match.
edgeCases: Maximum crop: (0, 0, 999, 799) on a 1000x800 image still keeps only rows 0-798 and columns 0-998. There is no way to express a crop that keeps the whole image; preserve this exactly (crop_manager.py:131-134 plus file_manager.py:728, 736).

Degenerate crop: if clamping collapses the rectangle so x1 == x2 or y1 == y2, the kept region is empty and the ENTIRE saved mask becomes zero, wiping every annotation from the export. Reachable from a drag: on a 100-px-wide image, press at x=99.4 and release at x=110 passes the >5 gate (width 10.6) but clamps to x1 = x2 = 99 (single_view_mouse_handler.py:553-556, crop_manager.py:132).

A drawn rectangle that is <= 5 px on either axis is silently discarded: no crop is set, no message is shown, the app STAYS in crop mode, and any previously active crop is left untouched (single_view_mouse_handler.py:548-558).
A successful drawn crop switches the app out of crop mode into the AI point mode (legacy mode name 'sam_points') (single_view_mouse_handler.py:557-558).

The active crop is cleared when another image is loaded (file_navigation_manager.py:279 -> main_window.py:2148-2156) and also when the SAM model is switched or unloaded (main_window.py:1261, 1287 -> 2956, 3003). It is never restored for a later image of the same size - that legacy restore is not being ported.

Multi-view has no crop. Applying, clearing or resetting a crop in multi-view calls _apply_multi_view_crop_coordinates / remove_multi_view_crop_visual (crop_manager.py:107, 88, 426), which are defined nowhere in the source and raise AttributeError, and the multi-view save builds its export context with no crop field at all (save_export_manager.py:504-514). Port as: crop unavailable in multi-view, multi-view saves never crop.

Sequence 'Save All' writes every propagated frame through the single-view save path while the on-screen frame's crop is still active, so the one active crop is applied to all of the frames it writes, and the mask dimensions come from the on-screen pixmap (main_window.py:4810-4813 -> save_export_manager.py:396-397, 412-417).

Clearing the crop drops it from the active state and from the size-keyed memory for the current image size, and restores full-image saves; it does not repair anything already written to disk (crop_manager.py:70-100).

If a crop removes every object, the NPZ is still rewritten as an all-zero tensor (npz.py:15-27 writes whenever mask_tensor.size != 0), while the other format files already on disk are left untouched because export_all never deletes (exporters/__init__.py:189-206). Stale labels are then left beside an empty mask.

Channel threshold, FFT threshold and rescale operate on image[y1:y2, x1:x2] when a crop is active - the same exclusive convention - and leave pixels outside the crop untouched in the displayed image (image_adjustment_manager.py:645-663; rescale via :393-394 and :622-623).

The crop blanking is never applied to the image fed to the AI/SAM model, and the crop rectangle is not part of the embedding cache key (image_adjustment_manager.py:637-638). Caveat: with 'operate on view' enabled the key is a hash of the displayed pixels (main_window.py:1580-1587), so changing the crop while a channel threshold, FFT or rescale is active does change the key indirectly.

Do not port or test against FileManager.save_npz / save_bb_txt (file_manager.py:47-49, 89-91) or SaveWorker (save_worker.py:76-79). They repeat the crop logic but nothing calls them; the only live application point is save_export_manager.py:412-417.
answer: Both open questions were decided on 2026-09-17. (1) SCOPE: a crop applies to the current image only and must NOT carry over to another image of the same size. Legacy does keep a size-keyed memory (crop_manager.py:144-145) and a restore block (file_navigation_manager.py:227-238), but I confirmed that block sits inside load_selected_image, whose only caller is main_window._load_selected_image (main_window.py:947, 1461-1463) bound to right_panel.image_selected, emitted only by file_tree.doubleClicked on a QTreeView that is constructed hidden 'for backward compatibility' (right_panel.py:117-122, 206); the shipping loader is load_image_by_path (file_navigation_manager.py:254-279), which calls _reset_state and nulls the crop (main_window.py:2148-2156) and never restores, and crop_manager.get_crop_for_image_size (crop_manager.py:408-413) has no callers at all - so neither the dictionary nor the restore is ported. (2) GEOMETRY: the inclusive clamp (crop_manager.py:131-134: x2 <= width-1, y2 <= height-1) combined with exclusive slice ends (file_manager.py:724-737) is preserved verbatim, including the unconditionally cleared last row and column, because exports must stay byte-identical. What was wrong in the card: the 'then' sentence 'so column 999 and row 700 are always cleared' conflates two different facts - in this example column 999 happens to be BOTH the crop's excluded end column and the image's last column, whereas row 700 is only the crop's excluded end row (the image's last row is 799, also cleared, by the bottom branch at file_manager.py:728-729); the always-true generalization is that the column at index x2 and the row at index y2 are excluded, and therefore the image's final column (width-1) and final row (height-1) can never survive an active crop (crop_manager.py:131-134 + file_manager.py:728, 736). The plainEnglish/parameters claim that 'crop corners are rounded' is misleading: round() at crop_manager.py:127 only ever sees integers, so the real conversions are int() truncation toward zero on the drag path (single_view_mouse_handler.py:554-555) and integer parsing on the text path (border_crop_widget.py:119, 126) - an implementer who writes Math.round will diverge on any sub-pixel drag edge, and Python's round() is half-to-even anyway. The 'parameters' string also duplicated 'x2/y2 exclusive in the mask' and buried the dead-loader nuance in a way that reads like a portable requirement; the >5x5 gate needed to be stated as strictly greater on BOTH axes, measured on the float rectangle in image pixels before truncation and clamping (single_view_mouse_handler.py:553); and 'and' was null though the full-image coordinate frame (yolo_detection.py:20, 29-32; exporters/__init__.py:107 never read), the copy-not-mutate semantics (file_manager.py:720) and the per-object intersection (segment_manager.py:297) all belong in the contract. The edge-case list carried three duplicates ('Multi-view saves ignore the crop' / 'Multi-view saves never crop', and 'Every crop drops its own last column and row' restating the full-image case) and was missing the reachable failure modes. What an implementer must watch for: the degenerate crop - once clamping collapses x1 == x2 or y1 == y2 the kept region is empty and the whole exported mask is zeroed, which a drag from x=99.4 to x=110 on a 100-px-wide image reaches despite the >5 gate; the silent no-op when a drawn rectangle is <= 5 px (crop mode is retained and the previous crop survives); the fact that a crop which empties the mask still rewrites the NPZ as zeros while leaving other-format label files on disk (npz.py:15-27, exporters/__init__.py:189-206); sequence 'Save All' applying the one on-screen crop to every propagated frame (main_window.py:4810-4813); and that multi-view must simply have no crop, since the legacy multi-view paths call methods that do not exist (crop_manager.py:88, 107, 426).
corrections: given: spelled out that the UI takes two ranges (X "-10:1200", Y "50:700"), parsed as bare integers with no validation and pre-swapped by the widget (border_crop_widget.py:115-135), and scoped the rule to single/sequence view.

then: replaced the ambiguous 'column 999 and row 700 are always cleared' with the exact kept region (rows [50,700) x columns [0,999), 650x999 = 649,350 positions per channel), named the tensor shape (800, 1000, numClasses) uint8, and stated explicitly that start coordinates are inclusive and end coordinates exclusive.
then/and: separated the example-specific clearing from the invariant - the image's last column (width-1) and last row (height-1) can never survive any crop, including the maximum crop (0,0,999,799).

and: filled in the previously null field with the copy-not-mutate semantics (file_manager.py:720), the full-image coordinate frame for all exports, the never-read crop_coords field (exporters/__init__.py:107), the per-object intersection (segment_manager.py:297), and the current-image-only scope.

parameters: replaced 'corners are rounded' with truncation toward zero on the drag path (single_view_mouse_handler.py:554-555) and integer parsing on the text path, and warned that JS Math.round diverges from Python's round().

parameters: restated the drawn-crop gate exactly - rectWidth > 5 AND rectHeight > 5, strictly greater, both axes, on the float rectangle before truncation and clamping - and noted typed coordinates bypass it.
parameters: removed the duplicated 'x2/y2 exclusive in the mask' clause and the redundant 'x2 <= width-1 and y2 <= height-1 by clamping' restatement.
parameters: turned the per-image-size memory from a described behavior into an explicit do-not-port instruction, per the 2026-09-17 decision.
edgeCases: de-duplicated the two multi-view entries and the restatement of the last-row/column loss.
edgeCases: added the degenerate crop that zeroes the entire mask, including the reachable drag that produces it.
edgeCases: added the silent discard of a <= 5 px drag with crop mode retained and the previous crop kept.
edgeCases: added SAM model switch/unload as a second crop-clearing trigger (main_window.py:1261, 1287 -> 3003).
edgeCases: added the stale-label hazard when a crop empties the mask (NPZ rewritten as zeros, other formats not deleted).
edgeCases: made the multi-view entry concrete - the legacy code raises AttributeError on undefined methods, so multi-view simply has no crop.

edgeCases: qualified 'crop does not affect the AI embedding key' - true directly, but with 'operate on view' the key hashes the displayed pixels, which the crop changes when a threshold/FFT/rescale is active.

edgeCases: made the sequence 'Save All' entry precise (one active crop applied to every propagated frame, mask size from the on-screen pixmap) and added an explicit do-not-port note for the dead save_npz/save_bb_txt/SaveWorker copies of the crop logic.
unresolved: Nothing blocks implementation. Two product decisions remain outside this card: (a) whether the inclusive-clamp/exclusive-slice off-by-one should be fixed in some later release that is allowed to break byte-identical exports, and whether datasets already exported with a crop would then be regenerated; (b) whether multi-view should ever gain a working crop, since the legacy multi-view apply/clear/reset paths call methods that do not exist and raise AttributeError.
